title: One-center assignment cut smaller-event temporal excess from 929 to 125-607 in global ComCat, 2001-2024
abstract: We tested how repeated use of smaller earthquakes changes pooled event counts around large earthquakes. We used a fixed ComCat snapshot, 1,093 centers with preferred magnitude M6.5 or more in 2001-2024, and targets with 5.5 <= M < 6.5. Targets were within 200 km through the Earth and 1 to below 30 days before or after a center. There were 1,951 after pairs and 1,022 before pairs, for a net of 929. These 2,973 pairs used only 1,389 distinct targets. Of these targets, 668 entered more than one center window. Assigning each target to its nearest eligible center in time gave a net of 505, a 45.6% reduction. Across every possible assignment to one eligible center per target, the net was from 125 to 607. Thus, positive temporal ordering survived every such assignment, but its count was always smaller than the pooled pair excess. The bounds are exact counting bounds, not confidence limits. At 300 km and on days 7 to below 30, the bounds include zero. Nine settings and a separate scalar count audit are included. This is a method benchmark for one retrospective catalog. It does not identify caused aftershocks, independent sequences, or a population triggering rate. Mixed magnitudes, location errors, event detection and selected windows limit physical inference. External event records are not bundled.

display.caption: Pooled pair excess and three one-center allocations. The second panel shows how many centers use each smaller target. All values describe one fixed catalog sample.
